newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise, bonds tumble on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise, bonds tumble on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended higher Thursday for the first time this week as investors shopped for bargains.
But bonds tumbled on profit-taking, dragging down the dollar against the German mark and Japanese yen.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 14.16 points at 6,437.10. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,273 to 1,223 on active volume of 483 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 3.10 points to 1,300.12.

"Bonds are selling off in anticipation of a strong jobs report after a tremendous amount of good news was absorbed," said Allen Sinai, chief economist at Lehman Brothers Global Economic Advisors. "Equities are gyrating after a tremendous run-up."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond plunged nearly 1-1/2 points, boosting its yield to 6.51 percent -- the highest since Nov. 8 -- from 6.40 percent at Wednesday's close.
"People are afraid of Friday's number," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

Payroll growth of 180,000 jobs is widely expected, but a few expect the figure at 200,000 or more, a number that could support the view that the economy might pick up in the fourth quarter after slowing in the third.
The jump in long-term interest rates sparked selling in financial and other interest-rate sensitive stocks.

But Sinai saw more good times for stocks. "It's still a bull market. The economy still looks terrific. Interest rates, even if they go up some, it won't be by a lot and the markets will adjust to that."
Stocks of some retailers weakened after reporting disappointing November sales going into the holiday shopping season.
The dollar fell to 1.5512 marks in late trading from 1.5605 late Wednesday. Against the yen, the dollar retreated as well, falling to 112.33 yen from 113.15.

In commodities, a surge in soybean oil exports coupled with already tight supplies sent prices for the oil sharply higher. Soyoil for December delivery rose 0.42 cent to 23.05 cents a pound at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Crude oil futures rose as bullish sentiment from tight supplies and a refinery workers' strike in Europe eclipsed the imminent addition of Iraqi oil on the market.

January crude oil rose 78 cents to $25.58 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange. January heating oil ended up 1.54 cents at 75.11 cents a gallon and January gasoline added 1.44 cents to 69.68 cents a gallon.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index closed 6.0 points higher at 4,051.2. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 average surged 283.99 points or 1.37 percent to finish at 20,943.90.
